A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RepoMem research. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original RepoMem localization experiments, memory and retrieval ablations, and cost and behavior analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds issue-resolution results, sensitivity tests, and operational measurements in Appendices A and B.

M1.justification: The episodic and semantic memories, four memory tools, BM25 retrieval, and LocAgent integration remain unchanged. Appendix A clarifies summary generation through LocAgent and dependency exploration; this is presented as further implementation detail, not a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: The SWE-bench-verified and SWE-bench-live dataset selections remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 adds actual end-to-end issue resolution on SWE-bench-verified, substantially extending evaluated task coverage beyond file localization.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain their main baselines and retrieval comparators. The new repair evaluation reuses CodeRankEmbed, Agentless, and LocAgent, while Table 8 extends the existing tokenizer comparison. CoRNStack in related work refers to the same Suresh et al. work, not a new baseline.

E3.justification: The original localization protocol is retained. Added experiments introduce an Agentless repair pipeline generating ten patches per issue, regression/reproduction-test reranking, and resolution-rate evaluation; a K sweep over 50, 100, 200, 300, and 400 files; and latency measurement on a random 50-instance subset.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds target-file coverage and localization sensitivity analyses for semantic-memory size, and extends the tokenizer ablation beyond Django to all repository groups. Appendix A adds construction-time, tool-latency, and response-length analyses. The original component ablations and failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new random 50-instance timing sample changes evaluation design, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical results. New results include 40.4% issue resolution for RepoMem versus 37.0% for LocAgent (Table 7), Django Acc@5 ranging from 74.4% to 81.0% across memory sizes (Table 6), additional standard-BM25 repository scores, and construction/latency measurements. These are added outcomes, not improvements over v1 under the original settings.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The existing Accuracy@k definition is retained; the new memory-size investigations are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged in substance, as are the introduction's contribution statements: commit-history-based episodic and semantic memory improves LocAgent localization. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a specific limitation concerning missing or noisy commit–issue links and reduced retrieval recall. It also discusses better history filtering, repository-specific memory sizes, diminishing returns, and downstream repair usefulness. Existing explanations of memory complementarity, sparse-history failures, and variable costs remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies dependency-aware summary generation through LocAgent, explicit commit–issue linking, per-file summary cost, and construction/runtime details. Appendix D supplies the existing agent task prompt in full. The reproducibility statement also promises code release, but provides no repository link.

R1.justification: A new Just-in-Time Software Defect Prediction subsection substantially broadens research positioning, distinguishing defect prediction from localization and grounding hotspot selection and historical linking in that literature. Relevant citations are added throughout the method and appendix discussions, while the Gutiérrez et al. memory citation is removed.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved, with localized wording edits. v2 adds related-work and disclosure sections plus supplementary appendices; the original tool-documentation Appendix A becomes Appendix C with unchanged content.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to the single-column ICLR format, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables and changed caption placement. Four new tables and the prompt Figure 9 are added; the original Figures 1–8 are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 establishes localization gains but leaves their downstream repair benefit and memory-construction overhead unmeasured. v2 addresses both with the common repair-pipeline comparison in Table 7 and operational measurements in Appendix A. Together with sensitivity tests, broader retrieval checks, and explicit construction and prompt details, these additions substantially strengthen practical validation and reproducibility. Statistical uncertainty and concrete code-access information remain unprovided.
